caseno: Writ Petition Nos. 554 of 1992, 661 of 1992, 1059 of 1992 and 1060 of 1992.
lawyer:
Khondkar Mahbubuddin Ahmed with Tofazzel Islam and ABM Bayazid, Advocates ----- For Petitioners in Writ Petition No. 554 and 1059 of 1992. 
S R Pal with Tofazzal Islam and ABM Bayazid ----- For Petitioners in Writ Petition Nos. 661 and 1060 of 1992. 
AF Hasan Ariff, Deputy Attorney-General-with Md. Fazlul Haque, Assistant Attorney-General ----- For the Respondent-Nos. 1-2 in all the petitions. 
Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed with Saifur Reza, Advocates - For the Respondent No. 3 in all the petitions.
parties:
Anwara Rashid and others ----- Petitioners [In Writ Petition No. 554/92]
Khodeja Begum and another ----- Petitioners [In Writ Petition No. 661/92]
A Bari Parvez Khan and another ----- Petitioners [In Writ Petition No.1059/92]
Majeda Khatun ----- Petitioner [In Writ Petition No. 1060/92]

full_judgment:
The petitioners are owners of 19 kathas of lands of CS Plot Nos. 12 and 13 of Mouza Dhanmondi having their two-storied residential building on the northern side of that land and the mosque and grave of their predecessor late Colonel MA 'Rashid to the southern side thereof. Respondent No. 3, Chairman Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakhya, in short, RAJUK required some land for construction of the link road connecting Green Road with Mirpur Road and the Planning Commission in its meeting dated 5.11.88 approved the scheme for 100 feet wide link road over the said building of the petitioners. Government on 12.11.89 informed the respondent No.1 Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka that subject to approval of Central Land Allocation Committee, in short CLAC proposal of RAJUK for 6.28 acres of land including 2.95 acres of private land approved for 80 feet wide link road with 6 feet wide footpath on both sides instead of 100 feet wide link road to save valuable land. Thereafter respondent No. 1 stated LA Case No. 40 of 1989-90 for acquisition of 2.95 acres of land belonging to the petitioners and others and issued notices and compensation payable to the petitioners for acquisition of their land and building was assessed on 14.11.89 by respondent No. 1. Thereafter construction of the said link road was ceremonially opened by the President on 30.12.89. CLAC in its meeting dated 12.2.90 approved allocation of 6.28 acres land including, 2.95 acres of private land. Thereafter the petitioner No.1 informed the respondent Nos. 1 and 3 that if the proposed link road is shifted towards the north petitioners' building as well as more private lands can be saved utilizing more Government khas land as per directive of the Planning Commission. Thereafter second revised drawing was prepared by RAJUK saving petitioners' building and sent proposal dated 9.4.90 to the Government to-obtain approval of the CLAC on the basis of 'the revised-drawing to save petitioners building by releasing some land from acquisition and by acquiring some land afresh and the same after approval by the respondent No. 4 on 10.4.90 was sent to the respondent No. 2 for obtaining approval of the CLAC. At that stage respondent No.3 being influenced by illegal occupants of Government khas lands to the north sent proposal dated 27.5.90, with revised third drawing dated 9.5.90 to respondent No. 3 shifting the link road to the southern side of petitioners building requiring 6.36 acres of land including 4.66 acres of private land. Petitioners filed objection to the said revised proposal dated 27.5.90 on the ground that almost entire land of the petitioners will be acquired and ground floor and entrance of petitioners building will be submerged by the earth work of the link road. Respondent No. 2 by summary dated 1.6.91 sought approval of the Acting President to the scheme. But by letter dated 14.8.91 Director President's Secretariat requested respondent No. 2 to supply particulars of khas land available near the proposed 80 feet wide link road and other particulars. But without furnishing the said particulars respondent No.4 prepared fourth revised plan dated 24.9.91 including therein petitioners building and some land to the south and as per the said drawing 6.40 acres of land including 4.68 acres of private land was required for the said link road and only small area of khas land was included in that plan, and RAJUK in its meeting dated 25.9.91 approved the same. Thereafter by letter dated 2.10.91respondent No. 3, requested respondent No. 4 to take up the matter with respondent No. 2 for allocation of the land by CLAC and to direct respondent No. 1 for requisition of land as the Prime Minister desired early implementation of the scheme arid there after respondent No. 2 took up the matter with CLAC which in its meeting dated 2.11.91 approved the allocation of 4.67 acres of private land as per revised drawing. Thereafter by letter dated 17.11.91 respondent No. 2 called back summary dated 1.6.91 from the Acting President's Secretariat, Thereafter on the representation dated 10.10.91 and 22.10.91 by a welfare society formed by the illegal Occupants of the Government khas land respondent No: 4 by letter dated 18.11.91 informed Prime Minister's Secretariat that necessary action in the matter was taken. Thereafter respondent No. 3 at the instance of interested quarters by letter dated 31.11.91 informed the respondent No. 2 that it is desirable to construct the link road as per 3rd revised drawing dated 9.5.90 falsely stating that CLAC in its meeting dated 2.11.91 allocated land as per third revised drawing dated 9.5.90. There after on 23.11.91 respondent No. 2 prepared and sent summary for the approval of the Prime Minister sending the 3rd instead of the 4th revised drawing and the Prime Minister approved the same on 25.11.91. Thereafter on 26.11.91 respondent No. 2 gave approval for acquisition of 4.66 acres of land under section 5(1) of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance. 1982 though till then no notice under section 3 of the said Ordinance was issued and formalities under section 4 thereof for hearing objection were not complied with. Notice under section 3 of the said Ordinance was issued on 28.11.91 after approval dated 26.11.91 depriving the petitioner’s opportunity to me objection and hearing in the matter. Petitioners received notice dated 19.12.91 under section 6 of the said Ordinance in the last week of December, 1991 acquiring their land without specifying the portion sought to be acquired. Petitioners also came to learn about notice dated 28.011.91 in the last week of December, 1991 after enquiry and obtaining a photo copy thereof. Thereafter petitioner No. 1 filed appeal to the Prime Minister to acquire land as per drawing dated 9.1.89. Comments having been sought -upon the said representation respondent No.3 came to the project site and assured the petitioners that steps are being taken to revise the acquisition line. But in spite of such assurance steps are being taken to construct the link road by the southern side of petitioners building as per drawing dated 9.5.90 and thereby frustrating petitioners appeal to the Prime Minister, Petitioners having no other alternative than to move this court. 

 3. Case of the petitioners in Writ Petition No. 661 of 1992 is as follows: Petitioner No. 1 is the owner of four-storied building on 5 kathas of land on the north western portion of CS plot No. 67 of Mouza Dhanmondi and petitioner No. 2 is the owner of two-storied building on 6 kathas of land on the north eastern side of the said plot No. 67. Respondent No. 2 by memo dated 26.11.91 gave approval to the acquisition of 4.66 acres of private land before compliance of formalities under section 4 of the said Ordinance and such approval under section 5(1) of the said Ordinance could be given only after hearing objection under section 4 of the said Ordinance but notice under section 3 of the said Ordinance was issued on 28.11.91. By taking wrong starting point from the northern side of CS plot No. 67 acquisition line has been shifted 25 feet south at the instance of interested persons. Without issuing any notice on the petitioners' fixing the demarcation line staff of the respondent Nos. 1 and 3 demolished the boundary walls of the petitioners on 4.12.91 and trying to put their buildings within the acquisition, though as per the revised drawing their lands do not come within the acquisition line. Notice dated 28.11.91 under section 3 of the said Ordinance was for collateral purposes at the instance of interested quarters. Petitioners filed objection on 8.12.91 and raised objection to demolition of their boundary walls and acquisition of their land situated on the further south side of the original acquisition line and also objected to the mode of survey conducted by the surveyors of the respondent Nos. 1 and 3 and requested for joint survey. Accordingly, on 24.12.91 a summary was made and claim of petitioners found correct and the survey made before issuing acquisition notice was wrong and the surveyor of the respondent No. 1 could not fix the demarcation pillar as per his survey due to opposition from the persons on the northern side of the link road and non-cooperation of the surveyors of respondent No. 3. Notice dated 28.11.91 under section 3 of the said Ordinance was suppressed and after demolition of their boundary walls the petitioners came to know about the acquisition. During pendency of their objection dated 8.12.91 respondent No. 1 issued notice dated 19.12.91 under section 6 of the said Ordinance showing acquisition of some land of the petitioners and their buildings thereon. Issuance of notice dated 19.12.91 before disposal of their objection and demolition on their boundary walls within the time for filing objection was malafide and for collateral purpose. 

 4. Case of the petitioners in Writ Petition No. 1059 of 1992 is as follows: Petitioner No.1 is the owner of about one bigha of land situated on the northern side of CS plot No. 12 of Mouza Dhanmondi and petitioner No. 2 is the owner of about 10 decimals of land in the south eastern side of CS plot No. 158 of Mouza Raza Bazar. Being unduly influenced by interested persons acquisition proceeding was started by issuing notice dated 28.11.91 under section 3 of the said Ordinance to acquire 24 decimals of land of the petitioner No. 1 and 10 decimals of land of the petitioner No. 2 for collateral purpose and in violation of the provisions of the said Ordinance and approval under section 5(1) thereof was given before issuing notice under section 3 thereof and hearing objection under section 4 thereof. In terms of the original plan only 0.05 acres of land of the petitioner No. 1 and 0.03 acre of land of petitioner No. 2 fell within the acquisition line. Petitioners came to learn about the proposed acquisition as per the 2nd revised drawing dated 9.5.90 in the 2nd week of January, 1992 and then they went to the office of the respondent No. 6 and obtained copies of notices under sections 3 and 6 of the said Ordinance. Thereafter on 22.1.92 petitioners filed objection against acquisition of their land as per revised plan and requested to construct the road as per original plan but no hearing was given to the petitioners. But without disposing of their objection and without payment of compensation to them respondents cannot construct the road. 

 5. Case of the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 1060 of 1992 is as follows: The petitioner is owner of about one bigha of land situated to tire northern side of CS plot No. 24 and north-eastern side of CS plot No. 67 of Mouza Dhanmondi. At the instance of interested quarters respondent No. 3 shifted the acquisition line of the land required for construction of the link road to further south on the basis of revised drawing dated 9.5.90 which was never approved by CLAC on 2.11.91 but CLAC approved the revised drawing dated 24.9.91. But respondent No. 2 by memo dated 26.11.91 gave approval for acquisition of 4.66 acres of private land under section 5(1) of the said Ordinance before compliance of formalities under section 4 thereof and notice under section 3 thereof was issued on 28.11.91 illegally for collateral purpose at the instance of interested quarters. As per the revised drawing dated 9.5.90 an area of 0.33 acre out of 0.36 acre of land of the petitioner falls within the acquisition line. Petitioner after coming to know about the proposed acquisition as per revised drawing dated 9.5.90 submitted on 24.12.91 a representation to the respondent No. 4, Additional Deputy-Commissioner (LA) Dhaka to reject the proposal of RAJUK as per revised drawing dated 9.5.90 as the acquisition was not in public interest but to benefit some interested quarters. Thereafter the petitioner went to the office of the respondent No. 6 and got copies of notices under sections 3 and 6 of the said Ordinance and filed another representation to the respondent No. 6 to drop the acquisition proceeding as per revised drawing. The respondent No. 6 without disposing of the objection of the petitioner and payment of compensation to the petitioner possession of the land cannot be taken over. 

 6. These Rules are being contested by the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 jointly filing one set of affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavit-in-opposition and respondent No. 3 by filing another set of affidavits-in-opposition denying the material allegations. Their case, in short, is as follows: An area of 2.95 acres of private land was acquired in LA Case No. 40 of 1989-90 by respondent No. 1 on receipt of approval for acquisition of the same and out of the same 2.41 acres of land was handed over to the RAJUK. Thereafter on 24.5.90 petitioner No. 1 made representation to the President to save her building and grave of her late husband from acquisition. Hence revised plan was prepared by the respondent No. 3 considering the objection of the petitioners to save their building and grave keeping in view engineering aspect and traffic facilities in the matter to make the road straight as far as practicable. 6. 36 acres of land was required for the link road including 2.95 acres of private land. But as a result of decision in 62 writ petitions 1.71 acres of private land was added increasing the area from 2.95 acres to 4.66 acres of private land. Neither the building nor the mosque nor the grave will be affected by the revised plan dated 9.5.90 which was approved and being implemented. According to the said revised plan, link road will pass keeping the building of the petitioners and the mosque and the grave on both sides of the said road. Ground floor and entrance of petitioners’ building will not be affected in any manner. CLAC allotted 6.40 acres of land in its meeting held on 2.11.91. CLAC having allocated .04 acre of land more than the required 4.36 acres respondent No. 3 by letter dated 21.11.91 informed respondent No. 2 about the said correction. Respondent No. 1 received only two drawings one dated 9.1.89 and the order dated 9.5.90 for the purpose of acquisition. Memo dated 26.11.91 issued by the respondent No. 2 intimating approval of the Government for acquisition of land was not the final decision as contemplated under section 5(1) of the said Ordinance. Rather it was the initial decision and as such words.  “১৯৮২ সালের ২ নং অধ্যাদেশের ৫(১) ধারার অধীনে” were inserted inadvertently in that memo dated 26.11.91 and the said memo dated 26.11.91 does not disclose of any objection under section 4 of the said Ordinance nor there was any such objection before respondent No. 2 and as such memo dated 26.11.91 is not a decision under section 5(1) of the said Ordinance and the petitioners cannot take advantage of the irrelevant insertion of the same. After receipt of the said memo respondent No. 1 served notice dated 28.11.91 under section 3 of the said Ordinance. Petitioners did not file any objection under section 4 of the said Ordinance but the petitioner No. 1 of WP 2554/92 filed a petition on 22.1.92 in response to notice dated 19.2.91 under section 6 of the Ordinance claiming compensation for the acquired land after service of notice under sections 3 and 6 of the said Ordinance correctly and according to law correctly writing the quantity of land acquired. Revised drawing was prepared and approved considering traffic problem, engineering aspect of construction of the link road, advantage and disadvantages of the people of the, locality and the affected persons, and in public interest and there is no malafide or partiality in the matter at the instance of any interested quarters. Petitioners of WP No. 2554/92 have no cause of action for the writ petition after filing of petition by the petitioner No. 1 for compensation in respect to notice dated 19.12.91 and the same is to linger the acquisition proceeding and to stop construction of the link road. Revised alignment was not made on the representations dated 10.10.91 and 22.10.91 of interested persons. CLAC did not approve drawing dated 24.9.91 but it approved drawing dated 9.5.90. Notice under section 3 of the said Ordinance was issued on 28.11.89 for acquisition of 1.32 acres of part of CS plot Nos. 8, 12, 15, 23, 24 and 65 of Mouza Dhanmondi and duly served in accordance with law in the locality as per the revised alignment but hearing objection was not necessary as the petitioners did not file any objection under section 4 (1) of the said Ordinance. No objection under section 4(1) having been filed by the petitioners and the area acquired by notice under section 3 of the said Ordinance being only 1.32 acres-less than than 10 bighas-there was no question or submitting report or obtaining approval of the Government. The petitioners cannot now object to the acquisition of their land. Similarly, petitioner No. 2 of Writ Petition No. 661 of 1992 filed another application on 4.1.92 to the respondent No. 6 claiming compensation for her acquired building at the present market rate. 

 9. Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners in some other petitions, submitted that Government gave approval to the acquisition of the land under section 5 of the said Ordinance before issuance of notice under section 5 of the said Ordinance depriving the petitioners of the opportunity to file objection and to be heard in the matter. He further submitted that by excluding Government khas land thereby shifting the acquisition line to the south on the land of the petitioners being unduly influenced by the unauthorised occupiers on such khas land in violation of the approval of the CLAC smacks of malafide and as such the whole acquisition proceeding is bad in law. 

 11. Mr. AF Hasan Ariff, learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the respondent Nos. 1 and 2, submitted that notices under sections 3 and 6 of the said Ordinance were-duly served according to the mode of service provided under rule 4 of the Acquisition of Immovable Property Rules, 1982 and the area to be acquired has been specifically mentioned in the said notice with specification of the land. He further submitted that petitioners having not filed any objection within 15 days of service of the said notice and some of them having claimed compensation long after such notice allegation of depriving them of any opportunity to be heard has no basis. Under memo dated 26.11.91 no approval under section 5(1) of the Ordinance was given as will be evident from the letter dated 9.8.91 of the respondent No.6 in reply to which the said memo dated 26.11.91 was sent. 

 12. Admittedly LA Case No. 40 of 1989-90 was started by the respondent No.6, Additional Deputy Commissioner (LA) Dhaka and 2.95 acres of land was acquired for construction of link road connecting Green Road with Mirpur road by the respondent No.3. RAJUK and after delivery of possession in 2.41 acres of the said acquired land to the RAJUK construction of the said link road was formally opened by the then President on 30.12.89. At this stage petitioner No. 1 of Writ Petition No. 554 of 1992 filed representations to the respondent Nos. 1 and 3 as well as to the President for saving her building and grave of her late husband from acquisition. But she has not annexed copy of the said representation with the writ petition to show what statement she made therein. However, the fact remains that to save the two storied building of the petitioners of Writ Petition No. 554 of 1992 the drawing of the proposed link road was revised but that drawing having created a big curvature in the said road alignment another revised drawing was prepared on 9.5.90 shifting the road alignment to the southern side of the petitioners' said two-storied building. This proposal with the revised drawing dated 9.5.90 was placed before the Acting President with summary dated 1.6.91 but the representation of the petitioner No. 1 having been sent to the RAJUK again the said road alignment was changed as per revised drawing dated 24.9.91. Petitioners contended that the proposal as per the revised drawing dated 24.9.91 was approved on 2.11.91 by, the CLAC but the respondents contend that the proposal as per revised drawing dated 9.5.90 was approved on 2.11.91 by CLAC. It appears from letter dated 21.11.91 sent by the respondent No. 3 to the respondent No. 2 that decision in the CLAC meeting held on 2.11.91 was not correctly recorded and in place of 4.67 acres of private land it will be 4.66 acres and total land will be 6.36 acres instead of 6.40 acres and the road should be constructed as per the alignment shown in the summary sent to the Acting President on 1.6.91. Thereafter summary dated 1.6.91 was called back from the Acting President's Secretariat and summary dated 23.11.91 was sent to the Prime Minister for her approval of the Scheme by acquisition of 4.66 acres of private land as per revised plan dated 9.5.90. It is admitted by the petitioners that this proposal was approved by the Prime Minister on 25.11.91 and fresh notice dated 28.11.91 under section 3 of the said Ordinance was issued for acquisition of 1.32 acres of land comprising parts of CS plot Nos. 8, 12, 15, 23, 24 and 67 of Mouza Dhanmondi after receipt of the approval of the respondent No. 2 dated 26.11.91 by the respondent No. 1. We are to see now whether approval of CLAC is a legal requirement for the acquisition of the said land. 

 13. It appears from Bangladesh Gazette published on 6.5.1976 that by resolution dated 27.4.76 Ministry of Land Administration, Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives (Land Administration and Land Reforms Division) formed Central Land Allocation Committee for approving proposals for allocation of land in the Dhaka City with Minister-in-Charge of the said Ministry as its Chairman, but this resolution does not state under what provision of law CLAC was formed. There is no provision in the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 requiring formation of CLAC and obtaining approval from CLAC for acquisition of land for public purpose or public interest. So it can be safely concluded that formation of CLAC and its approval is not a legal requirement but it has been formed for administrative convenience as a matter of policy to regulate acquisition of land under the said Ordinance. It appears from the said letter dated 21.11.91 of the respondent No. 3 that correction of decision of CLAC dated 2.11.91 was made with the approval of the Minister of State in charge of the Ministry of Land who was Chairman of CLAC. Subsequently summary sent to the Prime Minister pursuant thereto on 23.11.91 was approved by the Prime Minister on 25.11.91. Prime Minister being Executive Head of the Government if with her approval decision of the CLAC was changed then we find no ground to take exception to the same. 

 14. It is a fact and not denied that the respondent No. 6 issued notice under section 3 of the said Ordinance on 28.11.91 after receipt of the approval dated 26.11.91 from the respondent No. 2 along with the revised drawing dated 9.5.90. It is also admitted that as per this revised drawing dated 9.5.90 road alignment passed by the southern side of the said two-storied building and northern side of the grave and mosque over the vacant land of the petitioners of Writ Petition No. 554 of 1992 saving their residential building and grave from acquisition as prayed for. Thus we find nothing objectionable on the part of the, respondents in changing the road alignment as per revised drawing dated 9.5.90. To save the said building construction of the road in question was stopped for more than 2- and half years. When the petitioner No. 1's said building has been spared on her own prayer can she turn round now and claim that 'spare my valuable vacant land and take my building'. One cannot be allowed to blow hot and cold at the same breath. Law does not permit one to reprobate and approbate at the same time. We, therefore, find nothing malafide in the decision of the respondents to acquire additional land as per revised plan dated 9.5.90 excluding the said two-storied building, grave and mosque. Rather it is clear that the petitioners have not come with clean hands to challenge the acquisition in question. 

 18. From Annexure 3 to the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition it appears that by letter dated 9.8.90 respondent No.6 sent a detailed report to the respondent No. 2 in reply to the letter dated 1.8.90 of the respondent No. 2 explaining the details for purpose of acquisition of the land as per the revised drawing possibly dated 9.5.90 requiring 4.66 acres of private land. After receipt of that letter from the respondent No. 6 the respondent No.2 by letter dated 26.11.90 (Annexure M to Writ Petition No. 554/92) informed the respondent No. 1 that the Government approved the proposal for acquisition of 4.66 acres of private land under certain conditions. Thus, it is clear that this was an administrative approval pursuant to the approval of the Scheme by the Prime Minister on 25.11.91 and not any decision for acquisition of land under section 5(1) of the said Ordinance as wrongly mentioned in the said letter. Therefore, we find no merit in the submission on behalf of the petitioners that Government decided to acquire their land before issuing notice under section 3 of the said Ordinance depriving them opportunity to file objection and to be heard in the matter.
